# Umbraco Rules

Project conventions, enforced by code in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco` where possible. The short version of the ten UmbraCommandments.

1. **Never put content behind a composition.** Removing a composition permanently deletes its content on every document that used it — no recovery through revisions. Compositions are for meta, settings, CTAs. Litmus test: *if we remove this composition later, is what remains still viable content?*
2. **There are six kinds of document type — file each in its folder.** Page (renders), Block (renders; lives in block list/grid; never used as a composition), Composition (composed onto others; never rendered, never pickable), Data (element; never renders — settings, events, people), Repository (container node; never renders), Repository Item (the pickable records inside a Repository).
3. **Data types never sit at the root of the data type tree.** Built-ins under `/Umbraco/<editor>`, custom ones under `/Custom/<editor>`. `DataTypeSavedHandler` enforces this on every save.
4. **Register in an `IComposer`, not Program.cs.** If `IUmbracoBuilder` can do it, it belongs in `Composers/`. Non-Umbraco concerns (CORS, App Insights) go in `WebApplicationBuilder` extension methods.
5. **Production runs in production mode.** Umbraco Application Url set, `--configuration Release`, HTTPS only, no model generation, no template editing. `appsettings.json` ships configured this way — don't soften it; put dev conveniences in `appsettings.Development.json`.
6. **Aliases are English and camelCase.** No exceptions.
7. **Dictionary keys are PascalCase with dots** (`My.Dictionary.Item`), and a dictionary folder never has values of its own.
8. **Media always lives in a folder.**
9. **The content root only holds Repositories.** The site hangs under the WWW `siteRoot` node; going multi-site means adding another Page beneath it, not re-architecting. Because WWW never renders, the site Page needs a **domain** or nothing answers on `/` — assign `/` for a single site, a hostname each for several.
10. **uSync everything — commit `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/uSync/`.** Export is automatic; you should not need to trigger it. On Umbraco Cloud, use Umbraco Deploy instead.

value.markup:
MCP is open and community-driven. Any client can implement it, any tool can expose it, and nobody is locked in. That is what makes it stick: the protocol is the point, the vendors come and go.

If you haven't tried it yet, spin up a local MCP server for something you use every day. The first conversation is usually the best one.

Every document type, data type, block, media item and page on this site was created through the Umbraco MCP server. No backoffice clicks, no hand-written migrations — just a conversation with the management API.

That is the demo. The block grid you are reading right now was assembled block by block, one MCP tool call at a time.

    <CompressionEnabled>false</CompressionEnabled> <!-- Disable compression. E.g. for umbraco backoffice files. These files should be precompressed by node and not let dotnet handle it -->
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Umbraco.Cms" />
    <PackageReference Include="uSync" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <!--
      Opt-in to app-local ICU to ensure consistent globalization APIs across different platforms.
      Default mirrors prior behaviour introduced in https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco-CMS/pull/11276: enabled unless building on macOS without an explicit RuntimeIdentifier.
      To override:
        * Build/publish:  dotnet publish -p:UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu=false
        * Post-publish:   edit System.Globalization.AppLocalIcu in the published *.runtimeconfig.json
      Note: DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_APPLOCALICU is only honored when AppLocalIcu is absent from runtimeconfig.json

    <UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == '' and ($(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('linux')) or $(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('win')) or ('$(RuntimeIdentifier)' == '' and !$([MSBuild]::IsOSPlatform('osx'))))">true</UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu>

## What I built

A small **MCP-blog demo site**, entirely through the Umbraco MCP server, following AGENTS.md & UMBRACO-RULES.md (six folder kinds, siteRoot repository, English camelCase aliases, blocks rendered through Umbraco's own conventions).

**Content model** (created over MCP):
- **Document types**: `blogHome` (Page, renders, lists posts) and `blogPost` (Page, renders) in *Pages*; `siteRoot` updated to allow `blogHome` as its child.
- **Block element types** (in *Blocks*): `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`.
- **Data type**: custom `Blog Block Grid` (`Umbraco.BlockGrid`, 12 columns, all four blocks allowed) — `DataTypeSavedHandler` auto-filed it under `/Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid/` as Rule 3 expects.
- **Templates**: `blogHome` + `blogPost`, set as default/allowed templates on the document types. (`create-template` refuses content containing `&`/`?`, so I created the records empty and wrote the real Razor files to disk — the template records pick the file content up, confirmed by read-back.)
- **Media**: 6 Unsplash photos from `unsplash/` imported into a `Blog` media folder.
- **Content**: `Blog` (blogHome) under WWW with domain `/` assigned, plus 2 published posts, each containing 4-block grids (rich text + half-width image + quote + rich text), built with `create-document-block`.

**Razor rendering layer** (step 4, after stop→build→restart):
- `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` — pure adapters (`BlockGridItem<T>` → plain model → `Component.InvokeAsync`), exactly per the pipeline rules.
- `ViewComponents/` (Hero, RichText, ImageBlock, Quote) + `Models/Blocks/*` view models + `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml` markup.
- Page templates use `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks")`; the home page lists posts via `Model.Children<BlogPost>()`.
- Tailwind built (`npm install && npm run build` → `wwwroot/dist/site.css`).

## How to view it

The site is **currently running** on `https://localhost:44317`:
- **Home / listing:** `https://localhost:44317/`
- **Post 1 (Why MCP is Awesome):** `https://localhost:44317/why-mcp-is-awesome/`

- **Backoffice:** `https://localhost:44317/umbraco/` (dev login `admin@example.com` / `1234567890`)
- Photo credits appear in the image-block captions.

All five URLs return HTTP 200; block markup, media (`GetCropUrl` signed URLs → 200), and the Tailwind stylesheet all verify.

## Anything not working / notes

- **Order-of-operations gotcha (now resolved):** templates are precompiled into the assembly (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` + Razor build), so the empty template records produced empty 200s until the views were on disk and the app was rebuilt and restarted. The task's "reboot after modeling, then write Razor" ordering caught this; the current build is correct.
- The Umbraco startup log shows a benign warning about `UmbracoApplicationUrl` auto-detection being disabled (no impact on rendering), and the repository's pre-existing `SixLabors.ImageSharp` NuGet vulnerability warnings — neither is introduced by this work.
- No migration plan was written, per instructions; schema lives in uSync (`uSync/v18/` exports updated: content types, data types, templates, domains, media).
